title: PSN Down Before GTA 6 Launch: What Players Are Seeing
description: PSN down reports are spiking a day before GTA 6 launches on PS5, with login and download errors, according to Polygon. Here is what we know so far.

body.text: PSN down reports are piling up a day before Grand Theft Auto 6 officially launches, according to Polygon. PS5 players around the world are hitting login failures, connection errors and stalled downloads as demand for the game surges. It matters because this is the biggest release of the year, and the first big test of whether Sony's network can handle it.
Is PSN down? What players are reporting

Polygon says the launch is set for Thursday, Nov. 19 on PS5 and Xbox Series X, but trouble has already started. Players are seeing messages such as "Sony services are busy" and "Too many failed connection attempts," along with a mix of other errors.
Most complaints involve logging into PlayStation Network. There are also reports of server connection problems and trouble with updates and downloads.

There is a mismatch, though. Sony's official status tracker still showed the network as healthy when Polygon published. Meanwhile, Down Detector recorded a sudden jump in user reports about the service.
Polygon names a few codes players are running into:
According to Polygon, all of them point to the same cause: strain on PlayStation's servers. If you see one, the problem is likely on Sony's side rather than with your console or internet connection.
Why a single-player game still hammers the servers
GTA 6 does not need an online connection to play, but that does not spare the network. Players still have to download the game and its mandatory updates before they can start, as Polygon points out.

That would be true even with a disc. Polygon notes that seemingly all major games now need a day-one download for patches or security reasons. So millions of people are trying to pull hundreds of gigabytes at once.
Polygon puts the potential audience at 250 million people. It also notes that it was early afternoon in the United States, so many fans had probably just finished work and logged on at the same time.

Many PS5 owners tried to plan ahead by preloading the game from Nov. 10. Polygon says Sony likely saw trouble coming, since the company has publicly treated GTA 6 like a first-party release. Even so, the early preparation did little to stop the outages.

There is no timeline yet for when PlayStation's servers might stabilize, and Polygon says only that Sony is undoubtedly working on it. Watch for an update to Sony's status page, whether the error reports on Down Detector drop, and how smoothly downloads go once the game is officially live on Nov. 19. If you are planning a launch-day session, check your download status early and expect some patience may be needed.

faqs.a: According to Polygon, many PS5 players are reporting login, connection and download problems on PlayStation Network, and Down Detector is showing a sudden jump in reports. Sony's official status tracker still listed the network as healthy at the time of the report.

faqs.q: What do the PSN error codes WS-116449-5, CE-34861-2 and WS-37505-0 mean?
faqs.a: Polygon says all three codes point to the same underlying problem: PlayStation's servers are under serious strain. The article does not give Sony's own explanation for each code.

faqs.q: When does GTA 6 release on PS5?
faqs.a: Polygon reports that Grand Theft Auto 6 officially launches on Thursday, Nov. 19 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X. Some PS5 players were able to preload the game starting Nov. 10.
